lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Care and Basic Food Safety
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: cross-contamination basics

objective: With an adult, learners practice separating raw-food-risk items from ready-to-eat items using color-coded or labeled zones (cutting boards, plates, or containers) across two supported rounds, then explain the reasoning behind the separation.
scenario: With a trusted adult, the learner practices the basics of avoiding cross-contamination by keeping raw-food-risk items (or an adult-designated stand-in) physically separate from ready-to-eat items, using separate cutting boards or containers and separate hand-washing breaks between handling each type, guided fully the first round and leading the second with adult confirmation.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult is present for the entire practice, both rounds.
Hands are washed between handling the raw-food-risk zone and the ready-to-eat zone every time.
Stop and ask for help if any raw-food-risk item's condition seems unusual.

simulationAlternative.description: If handling an actual raw-food-risk item isn't appropriate for this household, the learner instead uses two clearly labeled stand-in items (for example a red-tagged item representing 'raw' and a green-tagged item representing 'ready-to-eat') to practice the same two-zone separation and hand-washing breaks, with the adult confirming the zones stayed correctly separated.

materials: a raw-food-risk item or adult-designated stand-in

tasks.directions: Before practicing, name one reason mixing a raw-food-risk item and a ready-to-eat item on the same surface could be a problem.

With your adult, set up two separate zones (or boards, or containers) — one for the raw-food-risk item, one for a ready-to-eat item — and practice moving between them correctly, washing hands between zones.

prompts.text: I used a separate surface or container for the raw-food-risk item the whole time.
I washed my hands after touching the raw-food-risk item and before touching the ready-to-eat item.
My adult confirmed the zones stayed separate throughout.
I did not set any ready-to-eat item down on a surface the raw-food-risk item had touched.

tasks.directions: Lead a second round of the same two-zone setup yourself, with your adult present to confirm, without being told each step.

prompts.text: Which part of keeping the zones separate did you remember on your own, and which part needed a reminder?

tasks.directions: Explain the risk of mixing zones.

prompts.text: Explain, in your own words, exactly what could go wrong if the two zones got mixed up — name a specific risk, not just 'it's unsafe.'

remediation: If the learner sets an item down on the wrong surface even once, reteach with a smaller, slower version — one item at a time with the adult narrating 'raw zone' or 'ready zone' out loud before each placement — before returning to the full two-round practice.
extension: Add a third zone (like a zone for washed produce) and have the learner reason through where it fits relative to the first two, explaining their placement to the adult.
